how_to_use.why:
- Uses readily available clinical demographic and laboratory values.
- More specific than CPK alone at predicting need for RRT (AUROC0.775 vs 0.631).
how_to_use.when:
- Patients ≥18 years old with rhabdomyolysis (CPK >5,000 U/L within 72 hours of admission).
- Do not use in patients with pre-existing end-stage renal disease or elevated CPK due to MI.
how_to_use.pearls:
- Can be used in both traumatic and atraumatic rhabdomyolysis.
- Not validated for patients who have had renal replacement therapy (RRT) within 24 hours.
- Not yet prospectively validated (has been[retrospectively validated](https://ccforum.biomedcentral.com/articles/10.1186/cc14363)).

next_steps.advice:
- CPK >1,000 U/L provides laboratory confirmation of the clinical diagnosis (CPK >40,000 U/L is used as a risk factor in the score).
- Delayed increase in CPK is common and therefore serial levels should be obtained.
next_steps.critical_actions: Les traitements néphroprotecteurs doivent être envisagés chez tous les patients jugés à haut risque (score ≥6), indépendamment du taux de CPK à l'admission.
next_steps.management: Le traitement néphroprotecteur doit inclure une réanimation liquidienne visant l’euvolémie et une diurèse d’au moins 1–2 mL/kg/hr.

Interpretation:

| McMahon Score | Risk group | Recommendation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| <6 | Low risk | Usual care (3% risk of death or AKI requiring RRT) |
| ≥6* | Not low risk | Initiate renal protective therapy including high-volume fluid resuscitation to urine output 1-2 mL/kg/hr (52% risk of death or AKI requiring RRT at scores ≥10) |

From[Simpson 2016](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pubmed/27259093).

*McMahon Score ≥6, calculated on admission, is 86% sensitive and 68% specific for identifying patients who will require RRT.
